title: NullReceiver: npm releases retrieving payloads through Ethereum transactions
description: Releases Sonatype identified as malicious in its analysis of a technique that hides the command-and-control address inside an Ethereum transaction: the package reads the recipient of a zero-value transfer and decodes the server address from it, so the address can be rotated on-chain without republishing the package. Each entry is a specific published version, in name@version form.
disclaimer: Third-party-reported, not independently verified per release by Chollima Hunter. These are version-pinned indicators on purpose: for a compromised legitimate package the name identifies the victim project rather than the threat, so a bare package name is not carried here, and the inclusion of a version says only that the cited report describes that release as malicious. Check the cited post before acting on any single entry.

source.title: Six npm Packages Use Ethereum Transactions to Retrieve Malicious Payloads

title: PolinRider: hijacked @adminide-stack and related npm releases (November 2026)
description: Twelve releases pushed between 3 and 4 November 2026 after the npm publisher accounts clockbook-app and pubngo-stack were hijacked, across ten established @adminide-stack, @cdmbase, @pubngo-stack, cdeops and server-hemera-mongo packages. None uses an install script: the PolinRider loader runs when the package entry point is imported, reads the latest transaction of Ethereum wallet 0x1eef0849eda15d87f64e51c73c8442cf3c8bcef3 for its C2 address, and fetches a Node RAT that persists by patching npm's cli.js and editor startup files. npm removed all twelve by 20:40 UTC on 4 November. Each entry is a specific published version, in name@version form.
disclaimer: Third-party-reported, not independently verified per release by Chollima Hunter. These packages are legitimate projects whose maintainer accounts were hijacked: the name identifies the victim project, not the threat, and only the version listed is reported malicious. Check the cited report before acting on any single entry.

source.title: PolinRider expands from npm into Go, Packagist, and Chrome extension supply-chain poisoning
